A dog waited for his owner at a train station for almost ten years.
In 1924, a professor in Tokyo took home an Akita puppy, and named him Hachiko.
Every morning, Hachiko walked the professor to Shibuya station.
And every evening, he was there waiting when the train came home.
But one day in May 1925, the professor died suddenly at work.
He never came home. Hachiko waited at the station anyway.
The next day, he came back at the same time. And the day after that.
Some workers at the station shooed him away. Others started bringing him food.
In 1932, a newspaper told his story. All of Japan fell in love with the loyal dog.
In 1934, they built a bronze statue of him at the station, and Hachiko was there to see it.
He kept waiting until he died, in 1935. Nine years and ten months after his owner was gone.
Today, Hachiko's statue is one of the most famous meeting spots in Tokyo.
